thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING oncall — high error rate and 5xxs from Cascade (customer) in their VPC dedicated pool (us-west-2). Impact: inference requests failing with connection resets and occasional OOMs. Paging severity: P1.

oncall_sre: I’m on it. grabbing logs and starting triage. what metrics are we seeing on the dedicated pool?

ricardo: errors spiking ~12:07 UTC, latency up ~800ms p95. seeing a subset of hosts with repeated `gRPC connection reset` and `CUDA OOM` in the runtime logs.

amanda: @oncall_sre fyi customer reported degraded production through support channel ~12:05. they’re seeing ~30% failures.

samir: placing a temporary token-based routing rule to stop new requests to the affected tenant-hosted nodes. will open canary to shared-hosts.

oncall_sre: executing drain on nodes that show OOMs. command:```bash
kubectl -n redwood drain node/cascade-dedicated-03 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```

incident-bot: deploy-bot: Canary rollout started for fallback model variant in us-west-2 (shared-pool).

ricardo: Logs excerpt:```
2026-03-14T12:06:51Z runtime[pid=4212]: gRPCStream reset by peer: code=14
2026-03-14T12:07:03Z runtime[pid=4212]: Allocation failed: CUDA OOM after 4096MB
```

amanda: reached out to Cascade support contact (Olivia). she wants ETA and whether requests are retried.

emma_support: drafting a short status note for customer now — will include that we routed traffic to a safe fallback and are investigating root cause.

oncall_sre: immediate mitigation steps: 1) isolate affected nodes (in progress), 2) route Cascade traffic to shared-pool fallback (done), 3) temporary qps limit per-tenant to prevent bursting (implemented), 4) collect heap/dump from failing nodes.

samir: added iptables rule to block egress to bad GPU nodes while we collect artifacts.

ricardo: I see a correlation between a config push at 11:58 and memory usage spike. pulling gitops diff.

oncall_sre: handoff: I need to hand this to morning shift. @samir do you want primary on investigation?

samir: I’ll take primary and will coordinate RCA. @oncall_sre please include the traces you collected.

incident-bot: incident-scoped channel created: #inc-1768301234-cascade.

amanda: internal execs are asking for a brief. @cto_ops want a 1-paragraph summary for the exec update.

cto_ops: short: Cascade experienced elevated failure rates due to CUDA OOMs on a subset of their dedicated pool hosts after a config change; traffic routed to shared fallback; no data exfiltration; working on RCA and customer remediation (credits/SLAs).

emma_support: customer note draft (first pass):
"Hi Olivia — we saw increased 5xx errors affecting ~30% of requests. We routed your traffic to a fallback pool to restore availability within ~3m and are investigating the root cause (possible memory configuration regression). We will follow up with a full RCA and proposed credit. Apologies for the disruption."

account_exec_julia: we should proactively propose a credit and timeline for RCA. ask for 72 hours for a full RCA draft and offer a one-time credit to make the customer whole for downtime.

samir: investigation update: diff shows `runtime.kv_cache.max_entries` was lowered in the last deploy which increased memory pressure for certain batch sizes. reproducing locally now.

oncall_sre: reproduction steps:```bash
# reproduce high memory usage
python tests/repro_batch.py --model llama-70b --batch 128 --seq 2048
```

rambling: observed memory climb to 98% without eviction. evidence points to mis-tuned KV cache + new attention kernel memory usage spike.

samir: proposed mitigation: revert the KV cache change for dedicated pools and push a hotfix that restores previous defaults. also add an automated guard in the deploy pipeline to prevent lowering `kv_cache.max_entries` below X for dedicated pools.

emma_support: updated customer note to add timeline and next steps. sending now and copying @account_exec_julia.

incident-bot: customer-outbound: message sent to Cascade (Olivia). message id 983412.

amanda: ops note: we blocked new allocations to hosts 03/04/07, drained 03, repro attached, routed traffic by 12:10 UTC. full restore to stable state by 12:12 UTC with fallback.

account_exec_julia: Cascade replied: thanks, want RCA and to discuss SLA credit. they emphasized impact on a live feature. asking for monthly credit + escalation.

cto_ops: ok, we should prepare: 1) 72-hr RCA draft, 2) proposed credit (X hours of dedicated capacity credit), 3) internal postmortem and mitigation plan, 4) customer exec call if requested.

samir: creating RCA draft now, will include timeline, root cause, mitigation, and long-term action items.

oncall_sre: tagging followups:
- samir: RCA draft (72h)
- ricardo: artifacts and logs upload to inc-1768301234 folder (ASAP)
- emma_support: customer comms and credit proposal
- account_exec_julia: coordinate credit + exec call
- eng-infra: add deploy guard for kv_cache param

ricardo: uploaded logs and heap dumps to s3://incidents/1768301234/ (link shared in #inc-1768301234-cascade).

emma_support: proposed credit language: "We propose a one-time service credit equivalent to 100% of the usage fees for the 30 minutes of degraded availability, applied to your next monthly invoice." thoughts?

account_exec_julia: sounds reasonable as a starting point. hold final approval until RCA confirms scope.

samir: RCA rough summary for review:
"Timeline: 11:58 deploy changed `kv_cache.max_entries` for dedicated pools. By 12:06 memory pressure led to CUDA OOMs on subset of hosts. 12:08 traffic routed to fallback, 12:12 stable. Root cause: unsafe config change that reduced cache headroom incompatible with the new attention kernel. Fix: revert config + deploy guard. Long-term: automated deploy-time static analysis for memory-sensitive params, and pressure testing for config changes in stage with realistic batch profiles."

oncall_sre: can we also add a runbook update for tenant isolation and a playbook for immediate routing to fallback? that would reduce time to mitigate in future.

samir: noted. adding runbook task to RCA action items.

emma_support: sent a follow-up to Cascade with proposed credit and offered a 30-minute exec call. asked for availability.

incident-bot: incident closed as P1 mitigated at 1768307890. post-incident follow-up channel remains open for RCA and customer comms.

amanda: thanks team — good coordination. leaving notes for postmortem meeting tomorrow 15:00 UTC.

account_exec_julia: scheduling exec briefing after RCA draft is ready.

cto_ops: please loop me into the RCA when ready. I’ll sign off on proposed credits once engineering confirms the scope.

samir: assigning owners in the RCA doc and will circulate for comments within 48 hours.

emma_support: will prepare the customer-facing RCA summary (one-pager) and share before the exec call.

oncall_sre: closing handoff. thanks all. :white_check_mark:
